questions.stem: What do we learn about the man from the conversation?
questions.stemZh: 从对话中我们了解到这位男士的什么信息?
questions.answerText: He has distinguished himself in foreign service.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Today's special guest is Lord Blackwell, one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats. 今天的特邀嘉宾是布莱克韦尔勋爵，他是我国最有经验、最杰出的职业外交官之一。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 主持人开场介绍嘉宾的那一句。答案信号是"访谈开场主持人对嘉宾的定性介绍"——one of our country's most experienced and distinguished career diplomats，访谈类对话里嘉 宾身份几乎都在开场这句一锤定音。

analysis.text: distinguished career diplomats ↔distinguished himself in foreign service diplomats（外交官）= foreign service（外交事务）的同义改写

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 未提及 录音里 Winopia 只是被问及的新闻话题，男方明确说自己 never been involved with Winopian relations（从未涉足对 Winopia 的事务），根本不是该国大使。选项 借"Winopia"这个反复出现的地名诱你误选。 借用原文：I've never been involved with Winopian relations C) 原词陷阱 男方说自己 I got a degree in electrical engineering，那只是早年学历，他随后转空军、 读法律、入外交界已 22 年。选项用 currently（目前）把旧学历说成现职，是典型"听到 electrical engineer 就想选"的原词陷阱。 借用原文：I got a degree in electrical engineering D) 未提及 通篇是主持人邀他来谈外交，男方对热点新闻还谦称只知道新闻上看到的，没有任何"爱出 风头"的迹象。He craves attention from the media. 在录音里毫无依据。

questions.stem: What does the man say the government of Winopia is probably undergoing?
questions.stemZh: 这位男士说Winopia政府可能正在经历什么?
questions.answerText: Some sort of crisis of legitimacy.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: It looks like the government of Winopia seems to be undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy, and an interim administration has been transitionally established until a head of state is agreed on. 看起来 Winopia 政府似乎正在经历某种合法性危机，已经过渡性地成立了临时政府，直到 选定国家元首为止。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 被问方对局势直接下定性结论的应答。答案信号是"被问者的直接应答"：主持人问 Winopia 现状，男方应答里直接给出定性 undergoing some sort of crisis of legitimacy，对话题答 案就落在这种"针对提问的正面回答"里。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: some sort of crisis of legitimacy ↔Some sort of crisis of legitimacy 答案句与选项几乎原句对应

analysis.label: 排除

questions.stem: According to the man, how does one get a career in foreign relations?
questions.stemZh: 根据这位男士的说法,如何获得外交关系方面的职业?
questions.answerText: Different people can take different paths.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: There are many different paths one can take. All diplomats have their own story. 可以走的路有很多条。每个外交官都有自己的故事。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 应答开头的总括句，先于个人举例。答案信号是"被问方应答的第一句总括"——There are many different paths one can take。它出现在男方随后讲自己经历（电气—空军—法 律）之前，总括句先于例子，正是答案所在；后面的个人路径只是举例佐证。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: There are many different paths one can take ↔Different people can take different paths many different paths = different people take different paths，多样性同义

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 与原文相反 录音 All diplomats have their own story 强调"各有各的"，选项 All diplomats have more or less similar stories to tell 借 All diplomats…story 的外壳，把 own（各自的） 偷换成 similar（相似的），意思正好反了。 借用原文：All diplomats have their own story B) 与原文相反 It is a prerequisite to get some practice in diplomacy. 把"实习"说成 prerequisite（必 要前提），但男方主张路径多样、从未说存在任何"必备前提"，绝对化表述与"因人而异"相 悖。 D) 原词陷阱 男方确实提到自己 obtaining a degree in international law，那只是他个人路径的一环。 选项 It is a must to first obtain a law degree. 把个人经历拔高成对所有人的"必须"，是听 到 law degree 就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：upon obtaining a degree in international law

questions.stem: What do the speakers mainly discuss by the end of the conversation?
questions.stemZh: 在对话结束时,说话者主要讨论了什么?
questions.answerText: Key skills required of a diplomat.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: W: What would you say are the key skills one needs for the job? M: There are so many. Being a hard worker and a good student is important... a diplomat needs to be very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric...people and communication skills are vital. 女：你认为这份工作需要哪些关键技能？男：太多了。做个勤奋的人、好学的人很重要…… 外交官在言辞和修辞上要非常善于表达……为人处世和沟通能力至关重要。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 结尾一问一答围着"关键技能"展开。答案信号是"结尾这轮问答的共同焦点"：主持人问 the key skills one needs for the job，男方随后整段都在列举各种 skills，问与答合起来锁定 主话题。主旨题靠这种"问答合判"，不靠单句。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: the key skills one needs for the job ↔Key skills required of a diplomat key skills…for the job = Key skills required of a diplomat，几乎逐词对应

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 过度推断 The making of an expert diplomat 谈的是"怎样成长为专家"的全过程，而结尾只在列举 工作所需技能，没讲成长路径。它把话题撑得比实际更大。 C) 原词陷阱 录音确说 articulate in their discourse and rhetoric，但那只是男方列举的众多技能中的 一项，Diplomatic discourse and rhetoric 拿一个细节当整段主题，以偏概全。 借用原文：very articulate in their discourse and rhetoric D) 未提及 结尾谈的是技能，没有讨论外交官做出了什么贡献。Contributions by diplomatic envoys. 在结尾内容里没有依据（envoys 一词虽前文出现过，但话题不是贡献）。 借用原文：our expert envoys at our consulate 1 M: It's getting late and we're both displaying signs of weariness. I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning. M: 时间不早了，我们俩都显出疲惫的迹象了。我觉得今天就到这儿吧，明天早上再碰头。 2 W: Oh, come on, Jeff. We are so close! Don't you think we are almost done? Let's do two more hours, please. W: 哎呀，别这样，Jeff。我们都快完成了！你不觉得马上就做完了吗?再干两个小时吧,求你了。 3 M: One hour, then I'm going home. M: 一个小时,然后我就回家。 4 W: OK, fine. I think we are making good progress, and that with a few more amendments, we will be all done. W: 好吧,行。我觉得我们进展不错,再修改几处,应该就全部搞定了。 5 M: I'm sure looking forward to it. I'm so tired of this project. Don't get me wrong. It's a great professional opportunity for me and a milestone for the company, but it's just been so long. M: 我当然盼着呢。我对这个项目真是烦透了。别误会,这对我来说是个很好的职业机会,对公司来说也是个 里程碑,只是时间拖得太久了。 6 W: Yeah. Two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough. Nevertheless, I think that with a bit of luck, we'll be done by next week. W: 是啊。两个月就做同一份合同,确实有点难熬。不过,我觉得运气好的话,下周就能完成。 7 M: Ha, you must be delusional. M: 哈,你肯定是产生幻觉了。 8 W: You don't think so? W: 你不这么认为? Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard. 9 M: No chance. Sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 still have to be aligned to the new framework. Then we need to proofread the whole thing and make sure all selling points are watertight. M: 不可能。第4、5、8和9节还得和新框架对齐。然后我们得校对整个文档,确保所有卖点都无懈可击。 10 W: But that will all take no more than a couple of days. W: 但那些最多也就几天时间。 11 M: I wasn't finished. When we are done with it and send it upstairs, what do you think will happen? M: 我还没说完呢。等我们做完提交上去,你觉得会发生什么? 12 W: What? W: 什么? 13 M: They'll argue about it for like a month. There's always going to be the odd board member who intervenes and demands rectifications be made. They might think they're being helpful, but in reality they're being obstructive and hampering progress. M: 他们会争论一个月左右。总会有某个董事会成员跳出来要求修改。他们可能觉得自己在帮忙,但实际上 是在妨碍进展。 14 W: Oh, Jeff, you're too preoccupied and cynical. It won't be anywhere as bad as that. You'll see, the entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible, and the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support. Go on then, let's stop there and meet up again same time tomorrow. W: 哎,Jeff,你太多虑也太悲观了。不会像你说的那么糟的。你等着看吧,整个管理层都想尽快实施这个项目, 董事会也几乎一致支持。那行,我们今天就到这儿,明天同一时间再见。

questions.stem: Why does the man suggest they call it a day?
questions.stemZh: 男士为什么建议他们今天就到此为止?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: It's getting late and we're both displaying signs of weariness. I think we should call it a day and meet again tomorrow morning. 已经很晚了，我俩都显出疲态了。我觉得今天就到这儿吧，明天上午再继续。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 提议收工那句里紧贴的理由状语。男方说 I think we should call it a day（提议收工）之前 紧跟着 we're both displaying signs of weariness（我俩都显出疲态），这个与提议直接 相连的状态描述就是收工理由，是答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: we're both displaying signs of weariness ↔They both look tired weariness 改写成 tired，displaying signs 改写成 look

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 They have got their work done. 借了原文反复出现的 done（如 we are almost done、 we will be all done）来诱选，但那些 done 都带 almost / will be，是『快完了 / 将会完 成』，并非已经干完；男方收工理由是累，不是完工。 借用原文：Don't you think we are almost done? C) 答非所问 They can meet again tomorrow anyway. 取自男方 meet again tomorrow morning， 但那是收工之后的安排，不是他『为什么要收工』的理由，与 Why 的问法错位。 借用原文：meet again tomorrow morning D) 未提及 They are both anxious to go home. 里 anxious to go home（急切回家）原文没有对应 表述；男方只说 call it a day（今天到此），是因为累，并未表现出急切回家的情绪。

questions.stem: What does the woman say is a little tough?
questions.stemZh: 女士说什么有点难?
questions.answerText: Two months devoted to the same contract.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough. 整整两个月只扑在同一份合同上，是有点难熬。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 题干同词 tough 在原文的复现处即落点。女方原话 Two months working on nothing but the same contract is a little tough 里出现了与题干完全一样的 a little tough，这个 评价词所修饰的主语就是答案句的核心。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: Two months working on nothing but the same contract ↔ Two months devoted to the same contract. working on nothing but 改写成 devoted to

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 张冠李戴 The board members' insufficient support. 里 board members 确在录音出现，但谈董事 会的是男方在 P13 段的牢骚，且女方在 the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support 反而说董事会几乎一致支持；把这话安到女方说 tough 头上，是张冠李戴。 借用原文：demands rectifications be made C) 与原文相反 Working two months without any progress. 多出的 without any progress 与原文相 反：女方明说 I think we are making good progress（进展不错），可见难的是『两个月 只干一件事』的枯燥，而非没进展。B、C 一字之差，差就差在这里。 借用原文：I think we are making good progress D) 张冠李戴 The man's long concentration on the project. 说的是男方对项目投入太久（呼应 it's just been so long），但题目问的是女方说哪件事 tough；把男方的体验安给女方所评价 的难事，主体错位。 借用原文：it's just been so long

questions.stem: What does the man say the woman must be in thinking they'll finish by next week?
questions.stemZh: 男士说女士认为他们下周能完成是怎样的想法?

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: Ha, you must be delusional. 哈，你一定是在痴心妄想吧。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 男方对女方乐观预期的直接回怼。女方在 we'll be done by next week 表达乐观，男方紧 接着 you must be delusional 直接回应——这句被问者 / 回应方给出的评价就是答案信 号，语气还带 Ha 的讥讽。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: you must be delusional ↔Delusional. 原句评价词直接成选项

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 偷换概念 Unprofessional. 与 delusional 同为贬义，易混；但 delusional 指『脱离现实、妄想』， 针对的是女方对工期的乐观判断，并非批评她职业水准。色彩对了，落点错了。 B) 与原文相反 Inspirational.（鼓舞人心）是褒义，与男方 Ha, you must be delusional 的讥讽否定语气 完全相反，听出语气是贬即可排除。 借用原文：Ha, you must be delusional C) 与原文相反 Exceptional.（出色的）同为褒义，男方并未夸女方，而是讥讽她想法不现实，褒贬方向就 不对。 借用原文：you must be delusional

questions.stem: What does the entire managerial hierarchy want to see according to the woman?
questions.stemZh: 根据女士所说,整个管理层想要看到什么?
questions.answerText: The early implementation of the project.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: the entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible 整个管理层都希望这个项目尽快落地实施。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: 愿望词 wants to see 直接领出答案。女方 the entire managerial hierarchy wants to see this project implemented as soon as possible 里 wants to see 与题干 want to see 完全对应，其后内容即所求愿望，是明确的答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: this project implemented as soon as possible ↔The early implementation of the project. 动词 implemented + as soon as possible 改写成名词 early implementation

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 原词陷阱 Fewer rectifications of the contract. 借了男方 demands rectifications be made 里的 rectifications，但那是男方预测董事会会要求修改的牢骚，不是管理层『想看到』的，且主 体是男方说的不是女方说的管理层愿望。 借用原文：demands rectifications be made B) 偷换概念 More support from the board members. 盗用 the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support 里的 support，但女方说的是董事会已经几乎一致支持，并非管理层『想要 更多支持』，把现状偷换成了诉求。 借用原文：the board, too, is virtually unanimous in its support D) 张冠李戴 The alignment of all sections of the contract. 盗用男方 Sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 still have to be aligned to the new framework 里的 aligned / sections，那是男方列举的剩 余工作，不是女方所说管理层想看到的结果。 借用原文：Sections 4, 5, 8 and 9 still have to be aligned to the new framework Section B 1 One thing I've learned in a quarter-century of management is that there are ample gray areas in human behavior, and that there may not always be clear right-or-wrong solutions to employee disputes. When two people have different versions of the same event, it can be hard to know whom to believe. One such circumstance always comes back to me. It happened years ago, and it's a measure of the forgettable nature of the conflict that I no longer even recall what the dispute was about, but I definitely recall the resolution. Two talented young executives, one of whom I was managing, had vastly different accounts of the same event, and it seemed likely we'd never get to the truth. We reached the deadlock, and the manager of the other individual said, "Here's something I learned from an excellent manager I once worked for. He used to say, 'When in doubt, assume positive intent.'" And just like that, we had a path forward. My counterpart and I agreed we might never ascertain the actual facts of the matter; quite likely there were elements of truth in both employees' stories. We agreed to monitor their actions and relationship going forward, but to intervene no further. We assumed the best about both of them and moved on. The result was that we were able to put the conflict behind us. In fact, their problems didn't Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard. recur. Over the years, this general approach has proved useful. Whenever the truth is obscure, assuming positive intent and agreeing to move on can be a constructive decision. 在担任管理职务的25年里,我学到的一点是,人类行为中存在大量灰色地带,对于员工纠纷可能并不总是有明 确的对错解决方案。当两个人对同一事件有不同的说法时,很难知道该相信谁。有一件事总让我记忆犹新。 那是多年前发生的,这场冲突之所以容易被遗忘,以至于我现在甚至不记得争议是关于什么的,但我确实记得 解决方法。两位才华横溢的年轻主管,其中一位由我管理,对同一事件有截然不同的说法,而且似乎我们永远 也无法查明真相。我们陷入了僵局,另一位员工的经理说:'有件事是我从曾经共事过的一位优秀经理那里学 到的。他常说,当你有疑问时,假设对方有善意。'就这样,我们有了前进的方向。我的同事和我一致认为,我们 可能永远无法确定事情的真实情况;很可能两位员工的说法中都有真实的成分。我们同意今后监督他们的行 为和关系,但不再进一步介入。我们对他们两人都做了最好的假设,然后继续前进。结果是我们能够把冲突 抛在身后。事实上,他们的问题没有再次出现。多年来,这种总体方法被证明是有用的。每当真相模糊不清 时,假设积极意图并同意继续前进可能是一个建设性的决定。

options.label: B
options.text: More support from the board members.
options.textZh: 得到董事会成员更多的支持。

options.label: C
options.text: The early implementation of the project.

In the early 2000s, researcher Eddie Yoon conducted a survey to ascertain Americans' attitudes to cooking. The survey found that 15% of Americans loved to cook, 50% said they hated to cook and 35% reported mixed feelings. When Yoon conducted the same survey 15 years later, only 10% of respondents reported a love of cooking, 45% said they hated it and 45% had mixed feelings. Yoon asserts cooking is akin to sewing. As recently as the early 20th century, many Americans sewed their own clothing. Today, the vast majority of Americans buy clothing; only a tiny minority still sew, and they do it mainly as a hobby. Yoon believes the number of home cooks will diminish in a similar fashion. Currently, the average American household spends over $3,000 per year on dining out. Making your own lunch, meanwhile, will cost less. One survey found people only spend on average $6.30 when they bring lunch prepared at home. And you've probably engaged in this behavior yourself. In a recent survey, nine out of ten respondents said they'd used their smartphone during their most recent social activity. There's also evidence that this behavior is socially harmful. It can leave people less satisfied with their face-to-face interactions. And it can generate feelings of resentment and jealousy. Now, the Journal of Applied Social Psychology has published a new study exploring the reasons for these effects. 你可能曾和某个在社交场合只顾玩智能手机而忽视你的人待在一起。而且你自己可能也有过这种行为。在 最近的一项调查中,十分之九的受访者表示他们在最近一次社交活动中使用了智能手机。也有证据表明这种 行为对社交有害。它会让人们对面对面互动的满意度降低。而且它还会产生怨恨和嫉妒的情绪。现在,《应 用社会心理学杂志》发表了一项新研究,探讨了产生这些影响的原因。 2 The study included 128 mostly female student participants. The participants watched a three-minute animation in which two cartoon figures interacted and engaged in a conversation. The conversation couldn't be heard but could be detected through mouth movements. Participants had to imagine themselves as the closest figure in the video and then make judgments about the conversations and how they felt about their conversation partners. 这项研究包括128名参与者,其中大多数是女学生。参与者观看了一段三分钟的动画,画面中两个卡通人物进 行互动并交谈。谈话内容听不到,但可以通过嘴部动作察觉到。参与者必须把自己想象成视频中较近的那个 人物,然后对谈话以及他们对谈话伙伴的感受做出判断。 3 In one version of the experiment, the phone of the participants' conversation partner remained unused on the table throughout the conversation. A third Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard. version involved the participants' partner alternating between periods of interaction with their phone and periods where they ignored their phone. They assert that the behavior is analogous to when people have no choice but to eat alone in the school cafeteria. The twist is that this exclusion occurs while sharing a physical encounter and having a conversation. Researchers found that the behavior had adverse effects on participants' sense of belonging, need for meaning and self-esteem. 研究人员认为,专注于自己的手机而不是关注同伴之所以会产生这种影响,是因为它被视为一种社交排斥的 形式。他们断言,这种行为类似于人们别无选择只能独自在学校食堂吃饭的情况。不同的是,这种排斥发生 在共享一次面对面接触并进行谈话的过程中。研究人员发现,这种行为对参与者的归属感、意义需求和自尊 心产生了不利影响。 6 These negative effects are similar to those caused by traditional forms of social exclusion. The new findings are important because they elaborate our understanding of a subtle but common aspect of our daily experience. analysis.text: Whatever the reason for traveling, a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations they find. 无论出行的理由是什么，旅行者们一个共同的抱怨就是他们遇到的那种缺乏人情味的住宿。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: complaint 信号词直接引出。答案句里 a common complaint of travelers is 与题干 commonly complain about 的抱怨信号严丝合缝，complaint 之后紧跟的 the impersonal accommodations 就是抱怨的对象，是典型的信号词后面接答案。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: a common complaint of travelers is the impersonal accommodations ↔ The impersonal accommodations. 近乎原句压缩

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 未提及 The ill treatment they get as tourists. 把抱怨说成受差待遇，但原文从头到尾说的是住宿 缺人情味、千篇一律，并没提任何被恶待、被歧视的内容，属于无中生有的升级。 B) 原词陷阱 The nonprofessional business they see. 借用了原文 personal or professional business 里的 professional 一词，但原文那句是说人们因私事或公务出行，根本没说他们抱怨不专 业的生意，是听到 professional 就想选的原词陷阱。 借用原文：many venture forth on personal or professional business D) 与原文相反 The many adventures on their way. 说一路有许多奇遇，是正面体验，而题目问的是抱怨 （负面）；原文也无奇遇之说，方向与抱怨正相反，自然不选。

questions.stem: What is said about Bed and Breakfast arrangements?
questions.stemZh: 关于家庭旅馆安排说了什么？
questions.answerText: They have been the classic way to visit Europe.

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe, especially the British Isles. And in fact, they are not really a new idea in America. 几十年来，B&B 一直是游览欧洲、尤其是不列颠群岛的经典方式。而且事实上，它们在美 国也并非真正的新事物。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: For decades 强调由来已久。For decades, B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe 用 For decades（几十年来）加现在完成时强调长期如此，与下一句 not really a new idea 一正一补都在说它由来已久、不是新事物，时间状语就是这里的答案信号。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: B&Bs have been the classic way to visit Europe ↔ They have been the classic way to visit Europe. 几乎原句搬运

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: B) 张冠李戴 They attract tourists with location and decoration. 说靠地段和装潢吸引游客，location 一词确在原文第三段 not only the building itself, but the location 出现过，但那是讲房主 开店要考虑的因素，不是说 B&B 整体靠地段装潢揽客，把后文的考量错安成对 B&B 的定 性。 借用原文：not only the building itself, but the location C) 未提及 They have long been competing with chain hotels. 提到与连锁酒店长期竞争，但原文 只说 B&B 提供个性化、友好的住宿来对抗千篇一律的感觉，从未提到 chain hotels 或彼此 竞争，属凭常识脑补出的内容。 D) 与原文相反 They are in fact a completely new idea in America. 说在美国是全新事物，恰与原文 they are not really a new idea in America 相反——原文明确用 not 否定了新事物，选项 却去掉否定取了反义，是漏听否定词导致的正话反说。 借用原文：they are not really a new idea in America

questions.stem: What is the first thing you have to consider if you want to start a B&B business?
questions.stemZh: 如果你想开办家庭旅馆生意，你首先必须考虑什么？

analysis.label: 定位
analysis.text: The first consideration is your property, not only the building itself, but the location. 首先要考虑的是你的房产，不仅是建筑本身，还有它的地理位置。

analysis.label: 信号
analysis.text: The first consideration 排序信号。The first consideration is your property 用 The first consideration 明示第一项考虑，与题干 the first thing to consider 完全对应，排序 信号词直接锁定 property。

analysis.label: 替换
analysis.text: The first consideration is your property ↔Your property. 原词直接对应

analysis.label: 排除
analysis.text: A) 答非所问 Your financial status. 财务状况听上去像开店头等大事，极易凭常识选中，但原文把财务排 在 The final consideration is a financial one——是最后一项而非第一项，错在排序。 借用原文：The final consideration is a financial one B) 偷换概念 Your family's consent. 说要家人同意，原文只说要考虑 the lifestyle of you and your family——家人是否真心喜欢接待客人，谈的是生活方式契合度，并非要谁点头同意，是把 原文意思偷换成了同意。 借用原文：the lifestyle of you and your family D) 答非所问 Your personality. 性格虽与原文 truly enjoy visitors（是否真心喜欢客人）沾边，但那属于 第二项生活方式考量，且原文用的是 lifestyle 而非 personality；它既非第一项、也不是原 文对首项的说法。 借用原文：truly enjoy visitors

A) Like most chefs, Flippy is not afraid of hard work. Since last summer, that has meant 11 am until 7 pm shifts at Caliburger in Pasadena, California, as well as short assignments at Chick-N-Tots at Dodger Stadium in Los Angeles. These are long hours of repetitive work, where the boss demands absolute consistency. But you won't hear Flippy complain or say anything, in fact. For Flippy is a robot — a cloud-connected mechanical arm with 3D thermal scanners for eyes — that can flip burgers or fry 80 baskets of food an hour, monitor that food and even clean up afterwards.
B) Flippy was created by Miso Robotics, part of the Cali Group, which is described by its CEO, John Miller, as: "A technology company that happens to sell cheeseburgers." Cali creates new machines that it road-tests in its Caliburger restaurants across the world, into which Flippy will be deployed this year. And Flippy is not alone. Also in California, Bear Robotics has developed a self-guiding robot, Penny, which has so far served 40,000 diners.
C) Ten years ago, robot-chefs and waiters were pure science fiction. Today, they are a reality, and at prices that make them a plausible investment. From May, Penny will be shipped on a subscription basis that offers "an immediate return", says Bear Robotics' chief operating officer, Juan Higueros. Flippy will cost a reported $60,000 to $100,000. Fully automated burger restaurants managed with minimal human oversight — where customers order at screens, pay electronically, and eat food cooked and delivered by robots — are now a possibility.
D) The technology exists; it just needs knitting together cost-effectively and in a way diners buy into. In an industry keen to slash labor costs and increase profits, further automation seems inevitable. After an eight-month test at Kang Nam Tofu House in California, Bear Robotics credited Penny with driving a 28% increase in sales. Meanwhile, in US trials, the self-ordering screens that McDonald's is currently installing at its 1,300 UK restaurants yielded a reported 30% rise in order values.
E) Personalisation is seen as key to the appeal of this technology, alongside its ability to reliably push so-called "upsells" (meal deals, extras, larger drinks) to customers. Soon when you log into a restaurant app, it will be able to use your data and purchasing history to recommend dishes to you — factoring in everything from the weather to, if you are ordering at a screen that can read your face, your mood.
F) "Right now people compromise on choice. We're presented with a one-size-fits-all menu. Ultimately, technology can allow us to make personal choices. You love spicy food and chicken? Here's the dish people like you mostly order," says Tom Weaver, CEO at the hospitality tech company Flyt. He talks enthusiastically about the Helsinki pop-up Take-In, a full-service restaurant where diners ordered dishes in from various delivery services. "For the first time in a few hundred years, digital is allowing us to create new versions of restaurants."
G) If high-street fast food is automation-ready, its impact on high-end restaurants is likely to be subtler and slower. "It'll probably be a very long time before we see a five-star robot-chef," says Noel Sharkey, professor of AI and robotics at the University of Sheffield. "Apart from the AI creativity gap, great cooking involves a subtle understanding of ingredients and delicate cooking that would be enormously challenging for robots. Placing fragile foods on plates would be incredibly slow."
H) Currently, robots have limited functionality. A human needs to load Penny with plates that diners lift off themselves. At the robot-powered US pizza-delivery company Zume, the more difficult jobs, such as topping pizzas, are still done by humans. But Moley, which will launch soon, offers an idea of the sophistication to come. Modelled on the movements of a MasterChef contest winner, Tim Anderson, its robotic arms are fixed over a stove and programmed to prepare dishes from raw ingredients. It is designed for domestic use, but a commercial version is planned that opens up the possibility of restaurant kitchens automating even highly technically challenging tasks.
I) For now, the kitchen technology that QSR Automations supplies to Mitchells & Butlers' pubs or KFC is less glamorous. Rather than having a chef shouting out diners' orders, the QSR system automatically distributes those orders across screens. The kitchen screens then tell chefs when to start cooking each dish, so that your plate of fish, chips and peas comes together at the right time.
J) The restaurant industry is currently suffering a severe shortage of skilled chefs — a deficit of 11,000, according to the skills agency People 1st. "Automation systems designed to make the process more idiot-proof are trying to bridge that gap," says Stefan Chomka, the editor of Restaurant magazine.
K) In terms of simplifying or enhancing the customer experience, online restaurant booking has been the easily-won success of the internet age. Automated at-table ordering and payment is seen as the next landmark. Until then, early adopters, such as the Manchester bar owner Andy Smith, who uses the Ordoo app at his venue 33 Oldham Street, may well experience growing but "lower than expected" acceptance.

The TGI Fridays drone(无人机) that injured a Brooklyn Daily photographer; US burger chain Shake Shack having to retreat from plans for entirely cashless ordering sites. P1 During his acceptance speech for the Nobel Peace Prize, Martin Luther King Jr. said, "I believe that unarmed truth and unconditional love will have the final word in reality."

P2 More than five decades later, our society is still struggling to separate truth from fantasy, fact from fiction. From disputes over the climate change to debates about how slavery is taught, America is at a crossroads. And the battle for equity is at the heart of these vital conversations.

P3 Study after study shows that inequity has had appalling consequences. A 2020 report by Citi indicated that "Black students could have increased their lifetime incomes $90 – $113 billion" if equity issues related to higher education had been adequately addressed over the past two decades. Questions 51 to 55 are based on the following passage.

P4 This statistic represents a flood of issues we've failed to confront as a nation. It also highlights one truth: We're missing out on valuable opportunities to bridge the differences that divide us. However, by honoring King's legacy, we can get our country back on the path toward true equity.

P5 Students — and adults for that matter — simply cannot understand the conflicts we have today without understanding what caused them in the first place. That means we have a responsibility to help them make connections between US history and current events. It also means giving them the tools they need to address inequity and bias in their own lives. Adherence to these principles, along with a commitment to truthful dialogue, can help every student better appreciate how far we've come and more clearly see the roads we have yet to travel.

P6 With more truthful analysis of the need for more qualified, diverse educators, we can improve our recruiting, training, and retention strategies for schools across the country.

P7 Unfortunately, our deeply rooted divisions are delaying these advancements. A recent survey found that 77 percent of Americans believe the nation is "more divided than ever before". But reports of increased polarization shouldn't persuade us to look away from one another. Instead, they should compel us to address our shared issues head-on.

P8 We are not, as some would suggest, living in a "post-racial society". We simply cannot afford to keep our heads buried in the sand when it comes to racial inequity. Unless we get honest about intolerance, bias, and how these social diseases impact the ways we treat one another, injustice will continue to haunt us. But our children and our grandchildren deserve better.

P9 On this Martin Luther King Day and beyond, let's commit to working together to disrupt the status quo. Let's continue to build a better, more inclusive nation; and in the words of Martin Luther King Jr., "A society at peace with itself, a society that can live with its conscience."

P1 Many see friendships as a comfort blanket: a shoulder to cry on, a reliable soul to confide in. However, more often than not, in our eagerness to seek individual success, we lose friends along the way and that has become part of the process.

P2 The chaos and never-ending turmoil that accompanies everyday life is an aggressive obstacle in the pursuit of stable friendships. As students, we use this excuse to shrug off losing people who we once thought to be loved ones.

P3 Instead of viewing our lives as a race, where everyone is on their own path to some form of success, we must relearn to value the connections we make along the track. We must reevaluate the harm of radical, individual freedom.

P4 Radical individualism elevates the freedom of the individual over the collective. It argues, for Questions 46 to 50 are based on the following passage. instance, that universal healthcare, an example of collectivism, threatened the dream of many Americans.

P5 Many of us have fallen victim to an individualistic culture. Society tends to celebrate personal achievement and commend it based on the assumption that winning or succeeding is a consequence of working harder than the next person.

P6 As a society, we idolize the concept of "losing friends on the road to success". I remember hearing in high school, "Don't worry about losing friendships, just focus on study and getting into college. That's all that will matter in the long run," a sentiment that is not unique to my experience. It's preached in many success stories, and it's embedded in the way we see growth. Motivational speakers will push their audience to be complacent to the inevitable end of losing friends. Spend too much time with friends? You're losing time better utilized on your achievements. Invest time in your relationships? Invest time in your work instead.

P7 This constant need to succeed has blinded us from seeing through the whirlwind of change that accompanies our everyday lives. We are expected to tangibly succeed, earn awards, get higher positions, earn better grades. In order to succeed, we lose friends, and that has sadly become normalized.

P8 We cannot be complacent with losing friendships because they are our anchors. Yes, pursue success. Challenge yourself. Push limits. But contrary to all the self-proclaimed success experts, doing it alone does not make you more successful or any better than someone who achieved it with the help of others.

P9 Put effort into fostering healthy relationships, and maintaining them through your busy schedule that seems like it leaves no time for anyone else. Although we may be living in a society that treasures the independent pursuit of achievement, having people to support and love you on the way is far more important than any end result.

Specifically, the rapid growth of technology, education and entrepreneurship offers a broad stage on which youth can turn their talents into real contributions. These opportunities become meaningful only when young people seize them actively. Take my cousin as an example: instead of chasing a comfortable office job, she founded a start-up that brings online courses to rural children. sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: In China today, this virtue is widely carried forward. 3. 社会各界积极营造敬老助老的社会氛围。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 社会各界营造氛围（主语策略：原句主语） 中文主语明确，提取 社会各界积极营造敬老助老的社会氛围 作主干：主语 People from all walks of life，谓语 actively foster/create，宾语 a social atmosphere。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 敬老助老作定语 敬老助老的 是修饰"氛围"的成分，降级成介词短语/定语 of respecting and helping the elderly 后置修饰 atmosphere，而非堆在名词前译成一长串前置形容词。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 陈述常态，回指基调用一般现在时 foster。 单复数 the elderly 表老年人群体，作复数概念，不加 s；a social atmosphere 单数加 a。 用词搭配 "营造氛围"地道搭配为 foster/create an atmosphere，"社会各界"用习惯说法 people from all walks of life 或 all sectors of society。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: People from all walks of life actively foster a social atmosphere of respecting and helping the elderly. 4. 为老年人提供便利服务已成为社会共识，例如社区专门开设长者食堂，公共场所配置优先 座位。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 提供便利服务成为共识（主语策略：原句主语） 主干取 为老年人提供便利服务已成为社会共识：用动名词短语 Providing convenient services for the elderly 作主语，谓语 has become，表语 a social consensus。后半的两个"例如"是举 例，归入降级处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两例并列举证 例如社区专门开设长者食堂，公共场所配置优先座位 是对主句的举例，用 for example/for instance 引出，两个例子是并列分句：communities open canteens for the elderly, and public places provide priority seats。可另起一句或用破折号衔接，避免与主句挤成一句残句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "已成为"含已完成意味，此处偏离基调用现在完成时 has become；举例的两件事是常态做法，用 一般现在时 open/provide。 单复数 举例的 communities、public places、priority seats 均用复数（泛指多个社区/场所/座位）； canteens 复数。 主谓一致 主语动名词短语 Providing… 视作单数，谓语 has become 用单数。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Providing convenient services for the elderly has become a social consensus. For example, communities open special canteens for the elderly, and public places provide priority seats. 5. 政府还出台了一系列政策，为老年人的权益提供有力保障。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 政府出台一系列政策（主语策略：原句主语） 主干取 政府还出台了一系列政策：主语 The government，谓语 has also introduced，宾语 a series of policies。后半"为老年人的权益提供有力保障"是政策的目的/结果，降级处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 目的成分降级 为老年人的权益提供有力保障 是"出台政策"的目的/作用，降级成现在分词短语 providing strong protection for the rights and interests of the elderly 作伴随状语，挂在主句后；不另起平铺一 个并列句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 "还出台了"强调已完成的举措，用现在完成时 has introduced，与上句 has become 一致地处 理"已经做了"的语义。 单复数 a series of policies 中 policies 复数；rights and interests 权益用复数固定搭配。 介词搭配 "为……提供保障"用 provide protection for…；"权益"惯用 the rights and interests of the elderly。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: The government has also introduced a series of policies, providing strong protection for the rights and interests of the elderly. 6. 尊老是社会和谐与发展的重要基石，有助于培育良好的社会氛围，推动整个社会文明进步。

sentences.label: 主干
sentences.text: 尊老是重要基石（主语策略：原句主语） 主干取 尊老是社会和谐与发展的重要基石：主语沿用 glossary 定的 Respecting the elderly，系 动词 is，表语 an important cornerstone of social harmony and development。后两个分句是 其作用，降级处理。

sentences.label: 降级
sentences.text: 两个作用并列降级 有助于培育良好的社会氛围，推动整个社会文明进步 是"基石"的两项作用，降级成现在分词短语 helping to foster a sound social atmosphere and promote the civilized progress of society，用 and 并列两个动词，挂在主句后作伴随状语，而非另起两个流水句。

sentences.label: 语法
sentences.text: 时态 陈述普遍意义，回指基调用一般现在时 is/helping。 主谓一致 主语 Respecting the elderly 动名词单数，谓语 is 用单数。 单复数与冠词 an important cornerstone 单数加 an；a sound social atmosphere 单数加 a；society 泛指社 会整体不加冠词。

sentences.label: 译文
sentences.text: Respecting the elderly is an important cornerstone of social harmony and development, helping to foster a sound social atmosphere and promote the civilized progress of the whole society. 英语六级 2025年12月·第1套 · 全卷构成 Part III Part III Part III Part III
